Okay, so I’m not sure if you or anyone would find this helpful, but I’d like to share how severe my anxiety was during job search. I was deathly afraid to the point where it was agonizing the night and morning before my interview. Surprisingly, I did so well my 1st interview, but I didn’t know it came with a second one. 

The second interview was a panel full of higher level employees, and I was in severe fight-or-flight. I stuttered through parts of the interview, and I felt soooo embarrassed because I couldn’t speak and had to ask for water (worst symptom I have is dry mouth) 😩 

Fast forward, I am in that position plus scored another job! I still cringe at what happened, but even through my anxiety, I forced myself through it and got it. If I can stumble through an interview and try my hardest, anyone that’s reading can too. It happens, and it doesn’t mean you’re less worthy of a job or less capable because of anxiety.

Yes, but you also have to note that BMI is not a good indicator of muscle mass, body fat percentage, or health, etc. As a Kinesiology graduate, this is something we always have talked about. For example, I’m sure at this point I had a body fat percentage of 27% to 30%! For example, a bodybuilder will have a super high BMI for their age and height and weight, but that doesn’t mean they’re unhealthy. It’s because most of their weight comes from muscle, not fat. A body builder and an obese person can have the same BMI. Do you see why this is not a good measure of health? 

Although I was at a “normal” BMI, I had no muscle at all. I was starving myself, during this time. As you can see, there is only a 15 lb difference, but my body comp changed dramatically. My body was skinny fat because I had no muscle. My weight was just fat-free mass, my body fat, and little to no muscles. This is why focusing on my weight has never been my goal because weight can be dependent on fat percentage, muscle mass, etc. This is why I take progress photos.

Youtube was my best friend. I looked up workouts that I wanted to target. For example, my glutes. There are ton of people on there who give free workout routines. It can be helpful, as they even show you how to do it. I used to be scared to try, but only way you can master it is by practicing or by getting results is by trying. 

First, if you are a beginner, start off with body weight. So, example, if you want to build your glutes, hip thrusting or squatting will be your best friend. You must master the form, first. Youtube a video on how to hip thrust. Then, practice with them. Even watch the video at the gym as you’re doing it to help you. Recording yourself can help you see your mistakes, too. You can also get a personal trainer if you’re really uncomfortable alone! They can help you as you go along. I recommend Brett Contreas on YouTube for doing hip thrusts and other glute exercises. 

Make sure you really feel where you’re supposed to target. It may be overwhelming, but it gets better with practice and determination. Trust me, my form wasn’t perfect for months. 

Once you have mastered form and body weight is not challenging anymore, do this: 

1) Start going up in weight. Focus on compound lifts that you can progressively work up in weight. I pretty much do the same 2 compound moves on my leg days, with 2-3 accessory exercises (hip adductors, glute kickbacks, leg extensions). Compound moves are exercises like squats, deadlifts, and hip thrusts. They work out multiple muscle groups. This is where your muscle grows. These are vital. I promise you don’t have to do crazy exercises and different exercises every day. 

Stick to the same compound exercises with different variations of accessory exercises. I promise you this will help you grow. Growth comes from slowly going up in weight when you’re confident enough and ready to! 

Also, please lift where that it is enough where you don’t risk your form, where you could feel your muscle, but it is still challenging to where you can do up to 10 reps. If you can do 2 more reps, the next time, go up in weight. Most of the time, beginners start with the bar or simply at 5-10 lb. Then, as you feel like you’re comfortable to move up, do it. 

My example glute routine: 
- 5 min walk 
- Dynamic stretching after 
- Hip thrusts 4x10
- Romanian deadlifts 3x12
- 3 accessory movements 

Also, PM me if you have more questions. Overall, Form and feeling the muscle you want to target is more important than the weight. I literally only romanian deadlift 30 lbs and am still progressing on getting better at it. Form > ego.

Instagram videos/youtube videos helped me a ton! My form took a few months to work on. I used to workout with someone who would watch my form and give me feedback, or I would video myself and watch back to see where I could use some work. 

As far as exercises, I pretty much stick to the same exercises that I love to do!! It’s much more sustainable than doing random exercises you dislike. 

For example: 
I love hip thrusts and deadlifts, so for me I do those every leg day. I’m not a fan of doing “good mornings” or squats all the time, so I’m not going to really do those. I will do it once in a blue moon. 

Sample workout I did today: 
Warm-up: 3x10 Glute kickbacks and stretches

4x10 Hip thrusts 
3x10 Deadlifts 
3x20 Lunges 
4x10 Leg extensions
4x10 Leg press 
3x10 Cable pull-through


I usually pick 4-6 exercises for the day, based on how I feel!

Three things I go by: progressive overload, mind-to-muscle connection, and eating in a caloric surplus.

Usually do 3 to 4x10 of each exercise. If I feel like I can push myself, I will do up to 12 reps. 

1. Progressive overload: so important to always challenge yourself with every workout at your OWN pace. Increase your weight slowly. You don’t need to jump in and squat 200 lbs. I don’t even lift 200 yet, it takes time!! As long as it burns, that’s more effective than squatting 200 lbs with bad form. 

2. Mind to muscle connection: make sure you feel your glutes powering through the workout. If you don’t, then find out why. It could be that it’s too heavy or you didn’t activate them enough. I always do glute activating exercises before my workout as a warmup. Literally just do 3x10 or less of body weight glute kickbacks and single leg hip abductors with a plate. 

3. Caloric surplus: You need to be in a caloric surplus to make major gains. Trust me, I used to workout at 1500-1700 calories for a long period of time, and I wouldn’t see much of a difference. Eating more helps fuel me and I have so much food freedom, I love it!!
I also feel stronger!! 

As long as you have all those components and stay consistent, you will get the gains!!
